prompt: A free Saturday, no obligations. What are you most likely to actually do?
helper: Answer with what you would really do, not what sounds impressive.

options.label: Take something apart, or build something that works
Make something — draw, edit, write, arrange a space
Meet people, organise something, get a plan moving
Read up on something properly, or help someone who asked

prompt: When a group works with you, what do they end up relying on you for?
helper: The thing people ask you for without thinking about it.

options.label: Working out why something broke
Making the output actually look and read well
Keeping everyone moving and deciding what comes next
Catching the detail everyone else skipped

prompt: You are handed a problem nobody has solved before. What is your first move?

options.label: Break it into pieces and test the smallest one
Find who is affected and understand their situation first
Pull the numbers and see what they say before guessing
Sketch three completely different approaches

prompt: How true is this: I would rather make something new than improve something that already exists.

options.label: Completely — a blank page is the best part
Partly — I like inventing, but inside real constraints
Not really — improving something until it is excellent is the craft
I care less about new and more about it working for people

prompt: You have to explain something difficult to a room. How do you feel walking in?

options.label: Good — persuading a room is a thing I enjoy
Fine, as long as I can show it rather than only say it
Comfortable one to one; a whole room is harder
I would rather write it down properly and let it speak

prompt: How do you feel about learning a technical tool well enough to be dangerous with it?
helper: Code, CAD, statistical software, clinical equipment — anything with a real learning curve.

options.label: That is genuinely how I like to spend my time
Yes, if it lets me make better work
Yes, if it makes me faster or more accurate
I would rather build judgement about people than tools

prompt: Someone explains how a company actually makes money. What is your reaction?

options.label: I want the numbers — margins, costs, where it leaks
I start thinking about how I would grow it
I want to know whether the product is any good
I mostly want to know who it helps

prompt: Where would you do your best work, honestly?

options.label: Long uninterrupted stretches at a desk, deep in one thing
A studio — messy, visual, work pinned on the wall
Out among people, in meetings, moving between things
Somewhere with real urgency, where I am needed on the spot

prompt: You have to learn something new and hard. What actually works for you?

options.label: Build a broken version and fix it until it works
Copy work I admire until I understand why it is good
Structured course, clear syllabus, work through it properly
Find someone already doing it and get myself in the room

prompt: Ten years from now, which sentence would you most want to be true?

options.label: I built things that a lot of people use every day
My work is recognisably mine
I run something, and the results are mine to own
Specific people are better off because I was competent
